subject: URGENT: GreenFlux production degradation — US-EAST1 traffic stuck during cross-region shift
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@greenflux.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@greenflux.com>, GreenFlux OnCall <oncall@greenflux.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:13:45-04:00
Subject: Production impact — US-EAST1 traffic not failing over cleanly

Jordan —

We’re seeing a significant production impact right now. Since ~08:45ET our traffic to the main inference endpoint has seen a ~40% throughput drop and p95/p99 latencies spiking above 700ms / 2.4s respectively. Error rate (5xx) has climbed to ~3.7%. Our systems show that a cross-region shift to US-WEST2 was initiated but a sizable percentage of sessions (roughly 30–35%) appear to be pinned to an AZ in US-EAST1 and are timing out or retrying repeatedly.

This is customer-facing (multiple homes reporting slow responses). Can you confirm whether Redwood sees the same traffic stuck in AZ1 and what immediate mitigation you can enact? We need ETA for full restoration, whether you can reroute remaining traffic to US-WEST2, and whether token-level accounting will reflect the retries so we can reconcile billing impacts.

I’ve attached a CSV of p99 samples and a session dump for one affected tenant.

—Chris
Chris Nolan
Head of Platform
GreenFlux Energy

Attachments: p99-latency-2027-05-29.csv, greenflux_session-dump-05-29.json
From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@greenflux.com>, Anita Rao <anita.rao@greenflux.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:22:03-04:00
Subject: RE: Production impact — US-EAST1 traffic not failing over cleanly

Looping you in — Chris, thanks for the heads up and the files.

Initial ask: can infra confirm whether the US-EAST1 AZ in question has any recent node drains or pool scaling events between 08:30–09:00ET? Hannah, please check the warm pool/KV cache warmup logs and any recent kernel crashes on the serving hosts.

Immediate mitigations I’m proposing while we triage:
- Trigger a policy-level split: shift remaining session weight to US-WEST2 (start canary @ 40% -> 70% over 10m).
- If we see session stickiness due to stale routing cookies, force a short 2-minute client-side TTL reflex (we can ask GF to clear their edge cache) and apply a server-side affinity purge for affected session tokens.
- If queue backlog persists, apply an emergency scale-up of Dedicated pool for GF (if committed capacity available) and pin a compatible quantized model variant to reduce per-token latency.

Vivek — want your sign-off to brief execs if this exceeds 1 hour. Marissa — please prepare a draft customer-facing note with the ask for cache clear and an apology.

I’ll take point on the bridge for GF and keep everyone posted.

-jb

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@greenflux.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:37:18-04:00
Subject: RE: Production impact — US-EAST1 traffic not failing over cleanly

Jordan / team — preliminary findings from the runtime side:
- Around 08:41ET we see an automated AZ drain event in US-EAST1 (control-plane initiated) correlated with a small kernel OOM on 2/12 serving hosts. Those hosts attempted eviction and restarted; their KV caches did not warm successfully which caused a sudden increase in KV lookups to slower disk paths.
- Continuous-batching queues backed up when those hosts started rejecting new inflight requests; the router retried several times which amplified client-side retries and the 5xxs.
- We also observed a model variant mismatch on a subset of requests (old float32 variant still pinned for some sessions) — likely due to an incomplete rollout during the drain.

Short-term mitigation we applied (09:30ET):
1) Forced rollover of routing policy: moved 45% of remaining session weight to US-WEST2 (canary).
2) Issued affinity purge for tokens older than 5m for GreenFlux tenant.
3) Pinned low-latency quantized variant (q4_0) for the active endpoint to reduce per-token CPU/GPU time.

Expected outcomes: we should see p95 drop under 350ms and p99 trending down over the next 10–20 minutes if retries stop. Full restoration depends on completing cache warmups on the restarted hosts (approx 25–40 minutes) or keeping traffic routed away.

I’ll keep the infra logs posted. If the customer can clear edge cache as Jordan suggested, that will speed up convergence.

—Hannah
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@greenflux.com>, Anita Rao <anita.rao@greenflux.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T10:02:51-04:00
Subject: RE: Production impact — GreenFlux bridge and exec note

Thanks team — and apologies to Chris and Anita for the disruption. Quick executive summary for outreach and next steps:
- Impact: partial cross-region failover left ~30% sessions pinned to drained AZ in US-EAST1; manifested as increased retries and p99 spikes.
- Immediate fix: routing split applied, affinity purge, pinned q4_0 model variant. Metrics show partial recovery (p95 down ~220ms as of 09:58ET).
- Customer ask: they want explicit accounting for retry churn and a credit conversation.

Action items:
1) Marissa: send the customer-facing note with operations steps and apology; include a request for edge cache clear.
2) Hannah/Infra: continue cache warmups; if warmups don't complete in 25m escalate to full traffic drain of the troubled AZ.
3) Jordan: please prepare a one-slide exec brief with timeline and ask (credits, SLA exception) if we look like >1.5 hours.
4) CS: schedule a follow-up call with GF for postmortem within 48 hours.

I’ll prepare a short note for execs (CTO + Ops Head) in case we need leadership alignment for credits. Jordan — if you want, push the routing to 70% canary now; Hannah, what’s the risk of 70%?

-vivek

From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@greenflux.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@greenflux.com>, GreenFlux OnCall <oncall@greenflux.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T10:18:07-04:00
Subject: RE: Production impact — US-EAST1 traffic not failing over cleanly

Appreciate the rapid response. Two asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether token-level retries will be itemized on the bill or we’ll see net token counts (we need a short reconciliation to send to finance).
2) If you escalate to draining the AZ fully, what is expected downtime for active sessions? We need to coordinate customer notifications.

Also, we’re happy to clear the edge cache if you formally request it from us (please send the exact TTL keys).

—Chris

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@greenflux.com>, Anita Rao <anita.rao@greenflux.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T13:02:10-04:00
Subject: RE: Production impact — US-EAST1 traffic not failing over cleanly

Chris —

Quick update: we moved the canary to 70% at 10:05ET after confirming queue depth decreased and retries subsided. Metrics as of 12:58ET: throughput back to 96% of baseline, p95 180–240ms, p99 ~430ms (continuing downward). We have NOT performed a full AZ drain yet — only local control-plane restarts happened earlier; the remaining hosts are warming.

Token accounting: we will provide a reconciliation file that separates original tokens from retry-generated tokens for the period 08:30–11:30ET; I’ve flagged this to Billing. We will treat retry churn as a mitigation credit discussion — I will pull together a recommended credit range and route for approval.

Next steps:
- CS to book 1-hour postmortem tomorrow (we’ll send calendar invite).
- We’ll deliver a short exec brief by 14:00ET today for leadership review.
- Attachments: runbook-reroute-v2.pdf (internal), and the session/p99 files we received.

Apologies again — we’re keeping this prioritized. Please confirm once GreenFlux has cleared their edge TTLs (recommendation: drop session affinity TTL to 30s for 15 minutes).

-jb
